questions.q: How do democracies usually break down in the modern world, according to the authors?
a: Through a slow weakening of institutions and norms
Through a sudden military coup followed by martial law
Through a single fraudulent election and mass protests
Through a foreign invasion that removes the government
questions.why: The overview says democracy today ends gradually, as institutions erode and political norms shift.

questions.q: What role do political parties play as gatekeepers of democracy?
a: They decide which candidates enter mainstream politics
They write the constitution and interpret its rules
They oversee elections and count the votes
They control the courts and appoint judges
questions.why: Lesson 1 says parties control access to mainstream politics by choosing which candidates to accept.

questions.q: How did Hugo Chavez dismantle Venezuela's democratic system?
a: He packed the supreme court, silenced media and jailed rivals
He canceled all elections and declared himself president for life
He dissolved the army and replaced it with foreign troops
He banned all political parties except his own
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists court packing, silencing independent media and exiling or imprisoning opponents.

questions.q: Which two advantages let Trump bypass the Republican Party's gatekeepers?
a: Fame and money
Military support and party loyalty
Legal expertise and experience in office
Media ownership and union backing
questions.why: Lesson 2 says his fame and wealth meant he did not need the party establishment's approval.

questions.q: What do the authors recommend for resisting authoritarianism?
a: Fight extremism within democratic limits and seek compromise
Use the same dirty tricks that extremists use
Boycott elections until the political system improves
Rely on the courts rather than political organizing
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns against fighting fire with fire and urges cooperation and compromise within democratic bounds.
